# Company 049 — Cloud / Software Reliability Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:049`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:049`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-049-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no production restart, scale, rollback, failover or infrastructure mutation.

## Business identity

Purpose: detect, explain and safely remediate reliability failures across applications, infrastructure, dependencies and cloud services.

Problem: logs, metrics, traces, alerts and deploy history are fragmented; operators lose time correlating symptoms, identifying blast radius and choosing safe recovery actions.

Value: earlier detection, evidence-based root-cause hypotheses, guided containment, lower MTTR and eventually policy-bounded automation with deterministic rollback and verification.

## Complete product tree

Observability Ingest; Service/Dependency Graph; SLO/SLI Manager; Anomaly Detection; Alert Correlation; Incident Timeline; Root-Cause Assistant; Change/Deploy Correlation; Runbook Automation; Restart/Scale/Failover/Feature-Flag/Rollback Adapters; Capacity Predictor; Reliability Scorecards; Postmortem Generator; Chaos/Recovery Drill Manager; On-Call Assistant; Status/Incident Communications; API/SDK; Embedded Reliability Agent; MSP Edition; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Cloud/Stack Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: metrics/logs/traces/events, topology, health, error budgets, threshold/anomaly alerts, dedup/suppression, incident grouping, suspected causes, dependency impact, deployment diff, remediation options, authorization/risk, step verification, rollback, evidence, postmortems, reliability trends and cost/performance correlation.

Customers: startups, SaaS, ecommerce, platforms, internal IT, MSPs, DevOps/SRE teams, enterprises, regulated operators and software vendors.

Verticals: web/SaaS, ecommerce, fintech infrastructure, health/education admin systems, marketplaces, media/streaming, industrial/IoT backends, developer platforms. High-risk/regulatory environments require stricter packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may ANALYZE incident context, infer likely causes, prioritize hypotheses and recommend actions. Deterministic policy/state machines own action eligibility, blast-radius limits, sequence, verification and rollback. Protected/high-risk infrastructure actions require explicit authorization.

Architecture: telemetry pipeline, topology/knowledge graph, time-series and event stores, anomaly models, change ledger, SLO engine, incident state machine, runbook registry, execution adapters, circuit breakers, action policy, verification engine, replay/simulation and LLM grounded in current evidence.

## Agent tree

Telemetry Analyst; Alert Correlator; Incident Commander; Root-Cause Investigator; Change Correlator; Runbook Planner; Capacity Agent; Recovery Executor; Independent Verifier; Postmortem Agent; Reliability Coach; Cost/Performance Analyst; Security Escalation Agent.

## Deterministic services

Collectors; metrics/log/trace normalization; dependency graph; alert dedup; SLO calculator; runbook engine; action locks; rate limits; canary/rollback; health checks; incident ledger; idempotency; timeout/retry; circuit breakers; maintenance windows; safe-mode/kill switch.

## Workflow tree

Signal → validate/freshness → correlate → open/update incident → map impact → investigate evidence → rank hypotheses → choose safe runbook → policy/authorization preflight → execute bounded step if allowed → verify → rollback/escalate on failure → close with postmortem/evidence → feed reliability learning.

## Integrations / API / data

Cloud providers, Kubernetes/container platforms, serverless, databases, CDNs, queues, CI/CD, feature flags, status pages, ticketing/on-call, source control, APM/observability systems, incident chat. APIs for topology, incidents, recommendations, runbooks, actions, verification and reliability metrics.

Data: telemetry, service graph, deploys/config changes, incidents, runbook outcomes, SLOs, capacities, dependencies, action evidence. Customer telemetry remains isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Hosts/services/telemetry volume, incidents, seats/on-call teams, automation actions, enterprise/private, MSP/multi-account, premium runbook/cloud packs and API usage. Distribution through cloud/DevOps marketplaces, MSP/SRE partners and developer ecosystem.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Infrastructure credentials are high sensitivity. Least privilege, read-only default, scoped temporary action credentials, change freezes, maintenance windows, blast-radius ceilings, independent verification, full audit, secret redaction, tenant/network isolation. Never let an LLM directly hold broad cloud authority.

## Failure / edge cases

Telemetry outage, false alert storm, monitoring blind spot, dependency fan-out, region outage, split brain, partial rollout, cascading retry storm, bad health check, database corruption, quota exhaustion, provider outage, network partition, clock skew, stale topology, action succeeds but telemetry lags. Unknown state must block dangerous automation.

## Scale / overlap

Single app → multi-service → multi-cloud enterprise reliability control plane. Overlap #43 cloud cost optimization, #51 data pipeline watchdog, #53 release autopilot, #66 AI security gateway, #82 backup verification. #049 owns runtime software/service reliability.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** event/evidence model, health/provider abstraction, action risk/authorization, topology, incident/recovery, idempotency, circuit breakers and kill switches.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already needs reliability/recovery/observability seams; reverse-map should ensure portfolio-scale isolation.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** multi-tenant telemetry isolation, adapter registry, SLO/runbook engine, action sandboxing.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer collectors/UI/cloud packs/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global telemetry fabric, fleet-wide anomaly learning and massive multi-region orchestration.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: ingest/topology/SLO/anomaly/alerts/incidents/RCA/change/runbooks/actions/capacity/postmortem/chaos/on-call/comms/API/MSP/enterprise.
2. Feature Tree: telemetry/topology/error budgets/correlation/impact/hypotheses/deploy diff/actions/verify/rollback/evidence/trends.
3. Customer Tree: startup/SaaS/ecommerce/platform/IT/MSP/SRE/enterprise/regulated/software vendor.
4. Vertical Tree: web/commerce/finance infra/health admin/education/marketplace/media/IoT/developer platforms.
5. Brain Tree: incident reasoning/recommendation; direct high-risk mutation prohibited without policy/approval.
6. Agent Tree: telemetry/alert/incident/RCA/change/runbook/capacity/recovery/verifier/postmortem/cost/security.
7. Service Tree: collectors/normalization/graph/dedup/SLO/runbooks/locks/limits/canary/health/idempotency/circuit breakers.
8. Workflow Tree: signal→correlate→incident→diagnose→plan→authorize→act→verify/rollback→postmortem.
9. Integration Tree: clouds/K8s/serverless/DB/CDN/queues/CI/CD/flags/APM/on-call/source control/status.
10. Data Tree: telemetry/topology/deploys/incidents/runbooks/SLO/capacity/actions/evidence.
11. API Tree: topology/incidents/recommendations/runbooks/actions/verification/metrics.
12. Monetization Tree: hosts/services/volume/incidents/seats/actions/MSP/enterprise/API/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: cloud/devops marketplaces/MSP/SRE/developer partners.
14. Automation Tree: detection/correlation/runbooks/verification automated; destructive actions tightly gated.
15. Moat Tree: incident/outcome corpus, topology patterns, runbook effectiveness, cross-stack integrations.
16. Platform Tree: observability assistant→reliability autopilot→runtime control plane.
17. Risk Tree: wrong remediation/cascade/credential abuse/false RCA/stale data/data leakage.
18. Scale Tree: app→fleet→multi-cloud/global.
19. Spinoff Tree: incident communication/runbook marketplace/topology graph can become modules; cost/release/backup remain adjacent companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: provider/health registry, Agency, protected actions, telemetry, incidents, recovery, resource governor.
21. Design-Now Requirements: normalized health/action/evidence/topology interfaces and isolation.
22. Build-Now Requirements: ensure Command Center observability/recovery can govern many isolated company runtimes.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: collectors/cloud packs/customer UI/pricing/marketplace.
24. Autonomous Mature State: most incidents detect/diagnose/contain/recover automatically within hard limits; humans handle ambiguous/high-blast-radius failures.

## Saturation result

Additional coherent branches converge into release, backup, security, data-pipeline or cost systems already represented elsewhere.

# Company 050 — AI Front-Desk Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:050`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:050`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-050-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no calls, messages, bookings, intake or external communications.

## Business identity

Purpose: provide a policy-governed digital front desk across voice, SMS, chat and web for answering routine questions, qualifying requests, scheduling, routing and collecting structured intake.

Problem: missed calls, inconsistent answers, scheduling friction and repetitive intake create lost opportunities and service delays, while uncontrolled AI can make promises, expose private data or mishandle emergencies.

Value: reliable always-available intake and routing with deterministic business rules, explicit escalation, channel continuity and auditable communication boundaries.

## Complete product tree

Voice Receptionist; SMS Front Desk; Web Chat; Website Widget; Appointment Scheduler; Intake/Form Builder; FAQ/Knowledge Assistant; Call Routing; Qualification Engine; Cancellation/Reschedule Flow; Confirmation/Reminder Service; Queue/Waitlist; Location/Hours/Service Catalog; Multilingual Layer; Emergency Escalation; Human Handoff; CRM Sync; Call/Conversation QA; Analytics; API/SDK; White-Label/OEM; Multi-Location Edition; Industry Packs; Managed Reception Service.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: caller/contact identity, consent, language, channel handoff, FAQ grounding, service eligibility, appointment availability, routing rules, business hours/holiday logic, intake schemas, qualification, callbacks, voicemail, transcription, summaries, handoff context, spam/abuse handling, emergency scripts, accessibility, opt-out, retention and audit.

Customers: local businesses, service companies, clinics/administrative practices, legal offices, home services, property managers, dealerships, salons/spas, professional services, SMBs, franchises, multi-location enterprises, agencies/MSPs.

Verticals: healthcare admin only with careful privacy boundaries, dental, home services, auto, legal intake, real estate/property, hospitality, beauty/wellness, education, financial-office reception, government/nonprofit information lines. Each needs domain terminology, emergency boundaries and compliance packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain understands natural language, intent, service catalog, FAQs, customer context and conversation continuity. It may ANSWER, ANALYZE, RECOMMEND, collect structured data and execute low-risk scheduling only under explicit rules. It must not diagnose, give legal/financial advice, make unauthorized pricing promises, bypass consent or conceal escalation uncertainty.

Architecture: channel adapters, speech recognition/TTS abstraction, deterministic intent/permission router, knowledge retrieval with provenance, scheduling connector, CRM/contact graph, consent/preferences, conversation state, policy pack, escalation engine, spam/security filter, QA/evaluation layer and protected communication/action gates.

## Agent tree

Reception Agent; Scheduling Agent; Intake Agent; Qualification Agent; FAQ/Knowledge Agent; Routing Agent; Reminder Agent; Translation/Localization Agent; Human-Handoff Agent; Spam/Abuse Agent; QA/Compliance Agent; Conversation Analytics Agent; Knowledge-Maintenance Agent.

## Deterministic services

Telephony/SMS/webhook adapters; business-hours engine; appointment availability; identity/contact lookup; consent/opt-out; routing tables; intake validators; reminder scheduler; rate limits; call recording/transcript policy; retention; emergency keywords; protected send/book/change gates.

## Workflow tree

Inbound contact → channel/security/consent checks → identify/anonymous state → detect intent/language/urgency → retrieve approved knowledge or deterministic service data → answer/collect/route/schedule if policy allows → confirm exact action → execute authorized low-risk action → provide receipt → sync CRM → evaluate quality → retain/redact per policy. Emergency/high-risk/uncertain cases escalate immediately.

## Integrations / API / data

Telephony, SMS, calendars, CRM, scheduling systems, practice/field-service software, support/ticketing, maps/location, email, knowledge bases, payments only as protected handoff, analytics. APIs for contacts, conversations, availability, bookings, intake, routing, handoffs and QA.

Data: contacts, consents, conversations/transcripts, intents, bookings, intake fields, routing decisions, handoffs, knowledge citations, QA scores. Sensitive content must be minimized, redacted and isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Per number/location/seat, minutes/messages, bookings, conversation volume, industry pack, white label, API usage, enterprise, managed service. Distribution through vertical software marketplaces, telecom/VoIP partners, agencies/MSPs, local-business channels and embedded OEM partnerships.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Call/SMS consent and recording laws vary; data minimization, channel authentication, spam/fraud controls, sensitive-topic redaction, least privilege, opt-out enforcement, emergency disclaimers, no unapproved outbound campaigns. Healthcare/legal/financial verticals need strict scope and specialist review.

## Failure / edge cases

Speech recognition failure, noisy caller, accents, abusive callers, identity ambiguity, double booking, stale availability, no staff available, emergency language, minors, accessibility needs, disconnected call, telecom outage, duplicate webhook, provider latency, unsupported language. Failures must preserve callback/handoff state without duplicate booking or messaging.

## Scale / overlap

Single-location receptionist → franchise/multi-location → embedded front-desk infrastructure. Overlap #45 autonomous support, #46 onboarding, #64 business inbox, #84 deliverability. #050 owns first-contact/reception/scheduling intake.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** communication-channel abstraction, consent/preferences, scheduling/action idempotency, conversation provenance, emergency escalation, company isolation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center communication/protected-action interfaces should stay channel/provider-neutral.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** telephony/SMS abstractions, consent store, scheduling connector contract, redaction/retention.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** phone numbers, voice models, customer integrations, industry packs, pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** carrier redundancy, global numbers, massive multilingual routing.

4. Vertical Tree: health admin/dental/home/auto/legal intake/real estate/hospitality/wellness/education/finance-office/nonprofit.
5. Brain Tree: conversation/intent/FAQ/intake/scheduling assistance; regulated advice and high-risk promises prohibited.

8. Workflow Tree: inbound→consent→intent→knowledge/action→confirm→execute→receipt→sync→QA/escalate.
9. Integration Tree: telecom/SMS/calendar/CRM/scheduling/vertical systems/support/maps/email/knowledge.
10. Data Tree: contacts/consents/conversations/intents/bookings/intake/routing/handoffs/citations/QA.
11. API Tree: contacts/conversations/availability/bookings/intake/routing/handoff/QA.
12. Monetization Tree: number/location/minutes/messages/bookings/packs/white-label/API/enterprise/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: vertical marketplaces/VoIP/agencies/MSPs/local business/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: routine answers/intake/scheduling/routing/reminders automated; emergencies/uncertain/high-risk escalate.
15. Moat Tree: vertical workflow packs, routing/intent data, integration breadth, evaluated conversation quality.
16. Platform Tree: receptionist→multichannel front desk→embedded customer-entry infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: bad advice/privacy leak/wrong booking/emergency miss/consent violation/spam/identity confusion.
18. Scale Tree: one location→franchise→enterprise/global channel network.
19. Spinoff Tree: scheduling/voice QA/vertical intake may become modules; support and inbox remain adjacent companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: communication policy, identity, consent, scheduling, provider registry, redaction, incidents, evidence.
21. Design-Now Requirements: provider-neutral communication/consent/action-confirmation interfaces.
22. Build-Now Requirements: maintain channel/action isolation and auditable outbound/inbound authority.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: telecom procurement/customer numbers/vertical connectors/voice personas/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: routine first contact runs continuously; humans receive high-context escalations for emergencies, complex judgment and protected actions.

Value: early anomaly detection, dependency-aware impact analysis, evidence-backed root cause, safe remediation guidance and trustworthy data-quality SLAs.

Architecture: connector/collector layer, schema/data-contract registry, time-series quality metrics, lineage graph, rule engine, statistical anomaly service, incident state machine, replay/backfill planner, reconciliation engine, provenance ledger, LLM for grounded RCA and explanation.

# Company 052 — Certificate-of-Insurance Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:052`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:052`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-052-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no insurance acceptance, vendor approval, certificate issuance or contractual/legal determination.

## Business identity

Purpose: automate collection, extraction, verification, monitoring and evidence for certificates of insurance and related coverage requirements across vendors, contractors, tenants, partners and projects.

Problem: COIs arrive as inconsistent PDFs/emails, expire frequently, contain policy/limit/endorsement details that must be compared against contract requirements, and create operational exposure when missing or stale.

Value: continuous visibility into insurance compliance, faster vendor onboarding, automated reminders, structured exception handling and auditable proof without pretending software replaces insurance/legal judgment.

## Complete product tree

COI Intake Portal; Email/Attachment Ingestion; OCR/Extraction; Insured/Carrier/Producer Resolution; Policy/Limit Verification; Requirement Template Builder; Contract-to-Insurance Requirement Extractor; Endorsement Tracker; Expiration/Renewal Monitor; Vendor/Contractor Portal; Deficiency Queue; Reminder/Chase Automation; Project/Location Coverage Matrix; Additional-Insured/Waiver Evidence Tracker; Carrier/Policy Validation Adapter; Compliance Scorecard; Audit Package; API/SDK; White-Label/OEM; Broker/Agency Edition; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Industry Requirement Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: named insured, certificate holder, producer/carrier, policy types/numbers, effective/expiration dates, limits, deductibles where relevant, occurrence/aggregate structure, additional-insured language/evidence, waiver/subrogation evidence, primary/non-contributory status, cancellation notice where present, project/location scope, contract requirement version, exceptions, renewals, reminder cadence, source document hash, review/approval and audit history.

Customers: construction/general contractors, property managers, landlords, facilities teams, procurement/vendor-risk teams, franchise groups, events, municipalities, staffing firms, logistics, brokerages, enterprises and compliance service providers.

Verticals: construction, real estate/property, facilities, events, logistics, hospitality, staffing, municipalities, healthcare administrative vendor management, education, energy/service contractors. Each uses different coverage requirements and terminology.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may understand policy/certificate language, map contract requirements to extracted fields, explain deficiencies and prioritize follow-up. Deterministic rules own required limits/dates/endorsement checks. Brain may not declare legal sufficiency, bind coverage, approve a vendor or interpret an insurance contract as final authority.

Architecture: document ingestion/extraction, insurer/producer/vendor entity graph, requirement template/version registry, deterministic coverage rules, contract clause extractor, expiration scheduler, exception state machine, communication draft workflow, provenance/evidence ledger and optional grounded LLM for document interpretation.

## Agent tree

COI Intake Agent; Document Extraction Agent; Entity Resolution Agent; Requirement Mapping Agent; Coverage Verification Agent; Endorsement Agent; Expiration/Renewal Agent; Vendor Follow-Up Draft Agent; Exception Coordinator; Contract Requirement Analyst; Evidence/Audit Agent; QA/Compliance Agent.

## Deterministic services

Document hash/virus scan; OCR/parser; field validation; date/limit/rule engine; requirement templates; vendor/project associations; expiration scheduler; duplicate detection; reminder idempotency; review state; immutable evidence; protected communications/vendor-status gates.

## Workflow tree

Requirement created/versioned → vendor/project assigned → COI requested → document received/validated → extract → resolve entities → compare policy types/limits/dates/endorsements to exact requirement version → flag deficiencies/unknowns → authorized reviewer resolves exceptions → reminders/renewals → updated certificate rechecked → compliance evidence retained → expiration reopens workflow.

## Integrations / API / data

Vendor management, procurement, contracts/CLM, property/construction platforms, ERP, CRM, email, document storage, broker/carrier services where available, ticketing, identity/SSO. APIs for requirements, vendors, documents, extracted coverage, compliance state, expirations and evidence.

Data: vendors, requirements/versions, certificates, extracted fields, carriers/producers, policies, endorsements, projects/locations, deficiencies, exceptions, reviews, reminders and evidence. Insurance documents are sensitive business records and remain isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Vendors/contractors tracked, certificates processed, locations/projects, seats, enterprise/private, broker/reseller edition, API/OEM, managed compliance service, premium vertical packs. Distribution via construction/property/procurement/vendor-risk ecosystems and insurance brokers/consultants.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Protect policy/vendor data, least privilege, immutable original-document hashes, no fabricated endorsements, explicit unknown state, review separation, audit history and configurable retention. Product provides workflow/verification support, not insurance or legal advice.

## Failure / edge cases

Blurry scans, altered PDFs, multiple policies on one COI, blanket endorsements, missing endorsement forms, ambiguous entity names, policy renewal gap, carrier merger, project-specific limits, umbrella/excess layering, claims-made vs occurrence, cancelled policy, duplicate certificate, requirement changed after receipt, fraudulent document. Ambiguity must route to review.

## Scale / overlap

Small contractor program → enterprise vendor insurance control → broker/embedded compliance infrastructure. Overlap #24 vendor risk, #52 owns insurance-specific evidence, #63 vendor onboarding, #23 contract obligations. Integration should share contracts/vendor identity but keep insurance logic domain-specific.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** versioned requirements, document provenance, vendor/entity isolation, recurring expiry workflows, evidence state and protected communication/status decisions.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center recurring obligations/document provenance/vendor-registry interfaces may need reverse-map support.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** document pipeline, requirement engine, scheduler, vendor/project mapping, review/exception state.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** carrier/broker connectors, customer portals, vertical packs, pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** carrier/network verification, benchmark requirement libraries and global insurance packs.

1. Product Tree: intake/email/OCR/entity/policy verification/templates/contracts/endorsements/expiry/portal/deficiencies/reminders/matrix/carrier/audit/API/OEM.
2. Feature Tree: insured/holder/producer/carrier/policy/dates/limits/endorsements/project/requirements/exceptions/renewals/provenance/review.

4. Vertical Tree: construction/real estate/events/logistics/hospitality/staffing/municipal/health admin/education/energy services.
5. Brain Tree: document/contract mapping and explanations; legal/coverage sufficiency determination not autonomous.
6. Agent Tree: intake/extract/entity/requirements/coverage/endorsement/renewal/follow-up/exception/contract/evidence/QA.
7. Service Tree: hashing/OCR/validation/rule engine/templates/associations/scheduler/dedup/idempotency/review/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: requirement→request→receive→extract→compare→deficiency/review→renew→evidence→reopen on expiry.
9. Integration Tree: vendor/procurement/CLM/property/construction/ERP/CRM/email/docs/broker/ticketing/SSO.
10. Data Tree: vendors/requirements/certificates/coverage/carriers/policies/endorsements/projects/deficiencies/reviews/evidence.
11. API Tree: requirements/vendors/documents/coverage/status/expirations/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: vendors/certificates/projects/seats/enterprise/broker/API/managed/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: construction/property/procurement/vendor-risk/broker/consultant ecosystems.
14. Automation Tree: extraction/rule comparison/expiry/reminders automated; ambiguous/legal approval gated.
15. Moat Tree: requirement packs, extraction accuracy, vendor/carrier normalization, deficiency outcome history.
16. Platform Tree: COI tracker→vendor insurance compliance→embedded evidence infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: false compliance, altered docs, wrong entity, missing endorsement, privacy leak, stale requirement.
18. Scale Tree: SMB contractor list→enterprise network→broker/OEM platform.
19. Spinoff Tree: insurance-document verification modules may be embedded; vendor-risk/onboarding stay separate companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: documents, provenance, vendor identity, recurring scheduler, policy rules, communications, evidence.
21. Design-Now Requirements: versioned obligation/requirement and document-evidence interfaces.
22. Build-Now Requirements: preserve generic recurring compliance/document verification primitives in Command Center.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: carrier/broker networks, portal UX, vertical packs, pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: certificates ingest, validate, monitor and chase automatically; humans handle ambiguous endorsements, suspected fraud and final compliance exceptions.

Further branches converge into vendor risk, vendor onboarding or contract obligation management; insurance-specific verification remains the coherent boundary for Company 052.
